correctness.rationale: Every H(n,5) is cubic, so a radius-r ball has at most 3*2^r-2 vertices for r≥1. Four rounds can therefore cover at most 22+10+4+1=37 vertices, excluding n≥19, while three rounds cover at most 15, excluding b≤3 for n≥8. The displayed source sequences were checked by exact BFS and satisfy both coverage and source-validity for n=7,...,15. Exhaustive center enumeration, even without source-validity restrictions, shows radii 3,2,1 leave minimum 2,4,5 vertices uncovered for n=16,17,18, so the last radius-zero source cannot finish. For n=7, radii 2,1 leave at least two vertices, excluding three rounds. An independent replay reproduced the boundary uncovered minima and witness validity. Thus the finite enumeration is exhaustive only for four explicitly bounded orders and the infinite tail is analytic.
